Subject: EU BYO Keying & crypto ops onboarding — recap + next steps

Hi Aisha & team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to walk through the high-level compliance needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of customer requirements (as we understood them):
- Data residency: inference logs and request metadata must remain in our EU tenancy (Frankfurt region).
- PII handling: redaction preferred at application layer; however, logging must avoid storing raw PII.
- Key management: customer-managed keys required for at-rest encryption of model artifacts and persistent payloads (CMEK / BYOK). HSM-backed keys preferred.
- Audit/logging: 1 year retention for crypto/key use logs; 7 years for certain audit artifacts (per legal).
- In-transit: TLS with mutual auth for any private deployment endpoints (mTLS for VPC/private).

Open questions we flagged today:
1) Do you require HSM (FIPS 140-2/3) attestation for key generation and wrapping, or is cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys acceptable?
2) Who on your side will be the key custodian (name + email) for the BYOK process and ticketing?
3) Any special rotation policy (e.g., 90 days) or is standard rotation acceptable?

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager with our BYO-keying options and a SOC2 evidence stub for quick reference.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with your security/infra engineers (30–45 min) — propose: Thu 2027-08-05 09:30 CEST.
- If HSM attestation is required, schedule a runbook review with Soojin (security) and our infra ops lead.
- Draft SOW language for CMEK/BYO flows (I'll loop in Marissa for procurement).

Please confirm the preferred time or suggest alternatives.

Cheers,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — helpful recap. Quick answers and clarifications from our side:

1) HSM requirement: We need HSM-backed keys with attestation for key generation and wrapping. Cloud KMS is acceptable only if it provides HSM-backed keys from a certified HSM (please state the certs).
2) Custodian: I will be the primary key custodian (aisha.gupta@eurafinance.com). Security team (security@eurafinance.com) will be secondary.
3) Rotation: Standard policy is annual rotation, but we do require the ability to rotate on-demand and maintain key version history for at least 2 years.

A couple more asks: 
- Can you confirm: will inference-level telemetry include any tokenized user attributes? We want to ensure PII never appears in logs in cleartext.
- We need confirmation on the storage boundary: are KV cache / ephemeral caches ever written to durable storage?

Thu 09:30 CEST works for the tech deep-dive — please share an invite and agenda.

Regards,
Aisha

Hi Aisha — thanks for the quick answers. I pulled together technical clarifications below; happy to cover these in the call.

1) HSM attestation & acceptable KMS products
- We support wrapping and importing customer keys that are HSM-backed in the major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS with AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys, Google Cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys). We can accept externally generated keys that you wrap with a hardware-backed wrapping key.
- Attestation: we can provide key-origin/certification statements and a log of KMS key IDs and ARNs. For FIPS/CC specifics, our security engineering can produce the HSM cert matrix for the provider you choose (we will attach that doc after the call).

2) Telemetry & logging boundary (PII concerns)
- Inference telemetry: by default we log request metadata (timestamps, model id, request size, token counts), routing decisions, and anonymized traces. We do not persist raw request content to durable logs unless explicitly enabled by the customer for debugging.
- For customers requiring stricter controls, we offer an option to disable request-content logging entirely and only retain minimal routing/metric entries. We also provide a configurable application-level redaction helper that runs before telemetry capture.
- KV cache: our runtime keeps KV cache in-memory on GPU hosts. Ephemeral KV shards are not written to durable disk in the hosted flow. In Private deployments we provide options to pin cache persistence; that would be a configurable setting and would default to disabled for your use case.

3) Key rotation & version history
- We support on-demand key rotation and maintain key version metadata for a configurable retention period (we can commit to 2 years for metadata in your EU tenancy). Actual key material lifecycle will follow your KMS provider policies; wrapped key versions are tracked in our audit logs.

4) Audit/log retention & export
- We can configure crypto/key-use logs to meet 1 year retention and export to your SIEM via secure shipping (S3 with VPC endpoints, or secure push to your logging ingestion pipeline). Longer archival (7 years) can be exported/ingested into your long-term retention solution; we can include that in the SOW.

Attachments: I attached our HSM-cert matrix and a short exporter playbook (stub).

Let me know if you'd like the call to split into two focused runs: (A) KMS/HSM runbook + attestations, (B) telemetry & retention controls.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee | Security & Crypto Lead, Redwood Inference
